item.name: updateinsurance — change one plan field (wrapped shape)

request.description:
Send ONLY the changed field plus its o_<field> original; echoing every attribute fails 'Another user has changed this insurance record'. The bare unwrapped <insplan/> child can fault 'Value can not be null' (9/8). The `sequence` attribute is NOT the plan's number here - AMD reads it as the PATIENT's insurance ORDER (insorder): sequence="2,1" sets Medicare-first; echoing a plan's own sequence on any other edit resets the patient order to that one plan (9/14/2026, pat17472393: a begin-date edit turned insorder 4,3 into 4). ins_update.update() drops it unless passed. PATIENT ORDER (10/6/2026, chart 12232248): sequence="2,1" sent through a plan that is END-DATED answers success="1" with <patient insorder=""/> - the order is wiped; the same call through an ACTIVE plan lands; an order cannot lead with an end-dated plan. ins_update.update sends the order as its own call through an active plan named in the order (leading plan first), verifies it, re-sends once, puts back an order that a field edit wiped, refuses an end-dated lead without writing, and never raises after a write.

Helper: ins_update.update(pid, insid, **fields) - sequence= goes through an active plan, verified (10/6/2026)
Captured: 9/3/2026; wrapped shape 9/8/2026; sequence = patient insorder 9/14/2026
Status: proven

item.name: Rebill a charge (frequency 1 first via updextrainsinfo)

request.description:
HTTP 204 = queued. ALWAYS set resubmissioncode=1 origrefnum='' via updextrainsinfo first (William 9/3: every rebill is an original claim). sequencenumber = first number of the visit's insorder. Verify insbilled flips to 0. ONE REBILL PER VISIT (William 10/6/2026): chargerebill rebills the whole claim, so amd.rebill_charge sends a VISIT + sequence once per script run - a repeat answers 204 'SKIPPED' and sends nothing (allow_repeat=True forces it); a later run is never blocked; every 2xx rebill is logged to registers/rebill_log.jsonl. Re-route = freq1_visit.reroute(vid, cid, order, seq) / `freq1_visit.py reroute <vid> <cid> <order> [<seq>]` (live; --dry): visit insorder by a no-rebill full-visit echo (resave.set_insorder), then ONE freq-1 reset + ONE chargerebill - never move_to_ins.move(cid, seq) + freq1_visit.run (two rebills).

request.description:
Captured from William's UI import 9/2/2026 (era_upload.py); proven 9/22/2026 with SYNTHETIC 835s built from paper EOBs (billing/paper_remits/build835.py). Response {issuccess, filename, filesize, filemd5checksum}; the check appears in GET /api/era/checks asynchronously (5 s to ~4 min; polling every 5 s drew HTTP 500s, poll every 10 s). Dedupe is by file MD5, not by TRN: the same bytes are skipped, a different file with the same TRN creates a NEW check. AMD matches CLP01 = the AMD claim number (8-digit visit id + sequence letter, e.g. 19442529A) to the visit and each SVC line to the charge by CPT; it reads ONE reason per CAS segment (a second triplet in the same CAS is dropped -> 'Contains invalid payment reason codes'); AMT*B6 is ignored (allowed = charge - adjustments); a claim with no SVC lines still matches the visit and shows chargecount / chargecode / insurancebalance but errors 'Procedure codes do not match' (chargedetailid -1) - usable as a probe; the check's systemcarrier is whatever AMD matched from N1*PR (often the visit's BILLED carrier), so a paper payer is posted with the ERA-linked addpayments carrying carrierid = the payer's plan on the chart.

Verify: on every live payment of the visit |paid| + sum(reason amounts) == fee. A plain addpayments (no ERA link) silently drops reason codes - never use it for an ERA line.

item.name: Zapier: Gmail attachment -> hydrate URL -> Google Drive 'Upload File' (native hydration, any size)

request.description:
Proven 10/5/2026 on 11 attachments 150 KB - 20.8 MB: Zapier hydrates its own URL server-side, so size does not matter. Pass NO new_name (Zapier appends the extension again -> 'x.pdf.pdf'); a 'File Lookup Error' means the hydrate URL aged out - fetch a fresh one with step 1 and retry. Reply carries the Drive file id, fileSize and md5Checksum (verify the local copy against it).

Helper: (connector calls) -> billing/era_input/fetch_scans.py drive
Captured: 2026-10-05

body.raw: {"step1": {"tool": "execute_zapier_read_action", "selected_api": "GoogleMailV2CLIAPI", "action": "attachment", "params": {"message_id": "{{gmail_message_id}}", "attachment_filename": "{{filename}}"}}, "step2": {"tool": "execute_zapier_write_action", "selected_api": "GoogleDriveCLIAPI", "action": "file", "params": {"file": "<results[0].attachment hydrate URL from step 1>", "folder": "1Fz90JGLa-s_QTw0RSuUdGnvQznxyGEHO", "convert": "false"}}}

item.name: Zapier code action: Google Drive file byte range as base64 (files over the Drive connector's 10 MB limit)

request.description:
Created with write_code_action 10/5/2026 (GET https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files/{id}?alt=media with a Range header, plus the metadata call). 4,000,000-byte slices -> 5.33 MB tool results, persisted to disk and joined locally; 21 slices for five 14.7-20.8 MB batches. A 6 MB slice was never tested (the Drive connector choked at 9.6 MB of JSON, so stay at 4 MB). Each call is one Zapier task.

Helper: billing/era_input/fetch_scans.py chunks <persisted tool-result files...>
Captured: 2026-10-05
